question.problem:
Given that $5a≡5b\,(\text{mod}\,10),$ which of the following statements **must** be true?

I. $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,2)$

II. $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,5)$

III. $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,10)$
question.worked_solution:
The division property of modular arithmetic states that for $k\ne 0,$ we have

$$
ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)\,⟺\,a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

We're asked to consider the following statement:

$$
5a≡5b\,(\text{mod}\,10)
$$

Notice that $\text{gcd}(5,10)=5.$

Applying the division property, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5a & ≡5b &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 5\cdot a & ≡5\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,5\cdot 2) \\ \cancel{5}\cdot a & ≡\cancel{5}\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{5}\cdot 2) \\ a & ≡b &  & (\text{mod}\,2)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
